primarySources.claim: Ampere A1 is Arm-based and Oracle Linux and Ubuntu platform images are supported.
OCI lists Oracle Linux 9 and Ubuntu 24.04 platform-image families for Arm shapes and currently directs Arm users to the standard, not Minimal, Ubuntu image.
OCI publishes Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 image release notes; an exact immutable release remains to be selected.
Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 are ARM64 LTS releases; 24.04 standard maintenance ends May 2029 and 26.04 ends May 2031.
Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 uses the glibc 2.39 package family.
Ubuntu 24.04 publishes a systemd 255 package family for ARM64; exact updated image build must be observed.
Ubuntu publishes containerd packages for ARM64, with release/update pockets that can differ.
Ubuntu publishes runc for ARM64 and the displayed ARM64 build can differ from amd64.
Oracle Linux 9 supports aarch64 and uses UEK on that architecture.
UEK 8 is available on Oracle Linux 9 aarch64 and is default for fresh Oracle Linux 9.6 installations; exact OCI image behavior must be inspected.
Oracle Linux 9 BaseOS publishes aarch64 glibc 2.34 packages; the moving latest repository is candidate evidence, not an immutable pin.
systemd provides the system and service manager/PID 1 boundary.
systemd defines unit execution, credential, sandboxing, and process settings that require real PID-1 tests.
systemd exposes cgroup resource controls whose effective behavior depends on the booted manager and kernel.
containerd 2.3 is the first annual LTS track and publishes ARM64 artifacts; an exact patch is not selected here.
Official containerd binaries are available for ARM64 and upstream requires checksum verification.
runc publishes supported release branches whose status must be re-evaluated at freeze.
runc is Linux-only, runs OCI bundles, and official releases are signed by project keys.
BuildKit 0.30 release artifacts include ARM64 builds and supply-chain metadata; no LTS claim is made.
BuildKit documents OCI/containerd workers, rootless operation, multi-platform output, and reproducibility controls.
resize2fs supports mounted ext4 expansion when the kernel/filesystem support it and does not resize the underlying partition.
xfs_growfs expands a mounted XFS filesystem; exact kernel/tool behavior requires real tests.
